name: Rooted Peelings with No Section-First Schedule
definition: Use the stored $294$-concept one-corner family $P$ with noncorner endpoint $1895$, and the $290$-concept support-four repair $M=B\cup\{157\}$ with corner endpoint $29$.
parameters: $P$ has dimension $12$ and VC dimension $3$; $M$ has dimension $12$ and VC dimension $4$. For coordinate zero of $P$, the complete relative deletion graph has $13$ states and six maximal orders, all stopping after seven deletions with $146$ opposite-section concepts.
properties: Each family peels to its marked endpoint, but no active coordinate admits a relative peeling to the endpoint-containing section. In every coordinate, every corner of the opposite section already lies in the overlap. The first family is two-connected, periphery-free, and Cartesian-prime and proves the sharp VC-dimension-three threshold; the second shows that making the endpoint a corner does not restore a section-first schedule.
